A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QuadSync work and contain 30 complete, readable pages, including Appendices 7–11. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of equations, proofs, figures, tables, and experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original ETH3D and EPFL evaluations, camera-pose reconstructions, and randomized-update, collinear-camera, and distributed-synchronization experiments in Section 5 and Appendices 10–11.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results, including Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–7.

M1.justification: QuadSync and Joint Opt. retain identical objectives, Tucker factorizations, ADMM-IRLS updates, initialization, and tensor-estimation procedures in Sections 4–5 and Appendix 9.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 11 ETH3D and six EPFL datasets, ETH3D SLAM near-collinear sequence, and synthetic collinear and distributed-synchronization scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments. Figures 1–2 and Tables 3–7 retain the same comparisons involving TrifocalSync, LUD, NRFM, MPLS, and MPLS combined with BATA or Cycle-Sync.

E3.justification: Preprocessing, graph-density filtering, retained-camera counts, calibrated evaluation, error metrics, iteration budgets, and synthetic noise and sampling settings are identical. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Appendix 10 retains the same randomized-update speed–accuracy analysis, collinear-camera noise tests, and distributed-synchronization studies. The near-collinear reconstruction in Section 5.4.3 is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical and uncertainty reporting is identical, including the error bars in Figure 4. No seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–7 retain identical results, including numerical errors, runtimes, completion rates, and qualitative camera-pose reconstructions. No result entries or reported findings change.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, rank characterizations, scale-identifiability results, derivations, and Appendix 8 proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.2 contribution list, and Section 6 conclusion retain the same claims about quadrifocal synchronization, joint synchronization, theoretical guarantees, and empirical promise.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations and limitations concerning measurement quality, dense viewing graphs, computational cost, collinear configurations, and distributed synchronization.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page footnote pointing to the dmiao153/QuadSync GitHub code repository; v1 provides no such pointer. This adds implementation-access information without changing documented implementation details. The PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or functionality.

R1.justification: The same 55 works are cited, with unchanged research positioning. Entries [4], [7], and [8] only update citation page references after text reflow; no cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 adds a one-sentence code footnote and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The main prose, terminology, section ordering, and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The new footnote slightly reflows pages 1–2, moving one line of Section 1.1 onto page 2 and updating citation page references on page 13. All figure and table displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The first-page code pointer supplies implementation-access information absent from v1, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. The scientific content and complete empirical record remain unchanged. The supported benefit is limited to documenting where code can be found; repository quality and availability cannot be established from the PDFs.
